write-the-skill-from-a-real-run.header: Write the skill from a real run
write-the-skill-from-a-real-run.description: the standard advises: "Complete a real task in conversation with an agent, providing context, corrections, and preferences along the way. Then extract the reusable pattern into a skill." A skill an LLM writes from general knowledge alone yields "vague, generic procedures" [1].

agentskills-best-practices.title: Agent Skills, Best practices for skill creators

the-agent-can-interview-you.description: Anthropic's skill-creator checks the current conversation for a workflow the user wants to capture, extracts answers from it first, then interviews the user to fill gaps [1].

googles-route.header: Run the task without a skill first: Google's route
googles-route.description: Day 3 suggests asking your most experienced practitioner to "narrate three workflows they do regularly", picking the most repeated one, running the prompts without any skill loaded, and drafting a SKILL.md from the transcript. It closes with "Resist the urge to let an LLM generate fifty skills on day one." [1] This agrees with the standard's advice to extract from a real run. It is Google's vendor guidance, not a measured result.

google-agent-skills-whitepaper.title: Singhal, Hernandez Larios, Dus, Nigam and Kolan, Agent Skills (Google whitepaper, Kaggle)

two-starting-points.title: Two starting points
two-starting-points.script: Say it is the third time and you are ready to write the skill. There are two good places to start: your own notes from earlier runs, the logbook pages of earlier dives, or a run with the AI that has just gone well, today's dive, while it is fresh.

capture-the-why.title: Capture the why
capture-the-why.script: With the fresh run, ask the AI to interview you before it writes anything: why that depth, why that order, what would have counted as failure. You want the skill to hold your intent and not only the steps, because steps without the why break the first time the situation changes.

while-he-still-knows.title: While he still knows
while-he-still-knows.script: Then let it write the skill in the same conversation, while the whole run is still in its context window. Tomorrow it will have forgotten, and that is the condition we started with. So that is your first step: pick one task you've explained three times, and turn a good run of it into a skill. In a coding agent, that is one sentence: ask it to turn this conversation into a skill.
